stage1.impression: A fir-lined niche with a pair of smoked-acrylic horn speakers on oak plinths, seen past dark tub chairs. The fir and the scallops from the downlights are the best thing in the frame. Everything else reads as CG: the floor is a flat brown plane, the chairs are crushed black blobs, and the seated guest is a smooth grey mannequin with no clothes, hands or face, not a motion-blurred person. The two Orb lamps at the frame edges are bare white balls, and nothing of the concrete, steel, glasses or records gives a sense of life or scale. The speakers read as dark glass display cases with grey boxes inside, not as cast acrylic with glowing edges. A magazine would see a generic hi-fi showroom corner, not a specific bar.

blocking_9: The seated guest reads as a person (clothes with folds, hands, hair, a believable motion blur), not a grey mannequin
The speakers read as thick cast acrylic: polished edges that catch the altar spots, clean reflections, batts diffused behind smoked acrylic rather than seen through clear glass
The foreground chairs and floor hold texture: velvet nap and a pool of light on the floor, with no region over a tenth of the frame more than half crushed
The shell (board-formed concrete, steel, fir beams) and the 200 mm step show in the frame, so it reads as Planet EARF and not as a generic hi-fi niche
The Orbs glow as tinted acrylic with a frosted liner, not as flat white blown spheres
Signs of life at the tables: a glass, the record out of its sleeve, a candle pool on an oak table

defects.what: The seated guest is an untextured grey mannequin with tube limbs and a smeared ball head; it reads as a placeholder, not as a blurred person
The foreground tub chair is crushed (crush_pct 59.7, median 1.4): a black silhouette with no velvet
The floor is a flat, featureless brown plane (lum_range 30.6) with no polish, no grain, no reflection of the plinths and no visible step
The left speaker reads as a dark glass box (median 35.6): the batts look like grey cardboard inside a clear case, and its edges do not glow
The Orb at the left edge is a blown white sphere cut by the frame
The Orb at the right edge is a blown white sphere cut by the frame
A cold, flat grey screen panel with a single white square; it reads as a whiteboard and is the coolest surface in a warm room
The sleeve against the plinth is a flat tan card with no print or edge wear
The ceiling and the shell above and around the niche are near black and unreadable; no concrete, steel or fir beams show
Downlight hot spots on the fir soffit nearly blow (median 237.8)

changes.problem: The seated guest is a smooth grey mannequin. More than anything else in the frame, it says render.

evidence.measured: uniform grey body (lum ~30 to 40), no cloth folds, no hands and no hair at 2x crop; the blur reads as a smudge on the head only

change.to: move the guest to a tub chair facing the altar in the mid-ground (seen from behind and three-quarter, half in the altar spill), with a dressed, textured figure (a dark knit, trousers, hair), and keep the blur on the head and the hands only

changes.expected: A person you read as a listener, with the blur reading as movement, not as a placeholder

changes.problem: The frame shows a generic niche and black chair backs. It does not show the shell, the step or the tables that make the place specific.

evidence.measured: the top 60 px are near black (median 9.0); the foreground chair is 10 % of the frame and crushed; no concrete or steel is visible

out_of_scope.request: Show the speakers' acrylic as thicker, with more visible tint and glowing polished edges, beyond what light can do
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' cabinet, its tint (Smoke) and its parts are fixed. Only the light on them may change.

out_of_scope.request: Give the niche or altar a more distinctive architectural form, so it reads as Planet EARF rather than a generic hi-fi alcove
out_of_scope.why: The niche, the altar and the room's design are fixed by the card. The camera (c2) can only show more of the shell.
